Several stocks witnessed heavy trading activity on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) during Thursday’s trading session, reflecting strong investor participation amid positive market sentiment.

Among the most actively traded stocks by volume were Vodafone Idea, Motherson Sumi Wiring India, YES Bank, Suzlon Energy, Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC), Ashok Leyland, along with select gold and silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs). High trading volumes generally indicate increased investor interest but do not necessarily imply bullish or bearish price movement.

...

## What Are the Most Traded Stocks?

Most traded stocks are securities that record the highest trading volumes during a market session. High volumes can result from:

- Quarterly earnings
- Corporate announcements
- Sector-specific developments
- Broader market sentiment
- Institutional buying or selling
- Increased retail participation

Trading volume is an important market indicator because it reflects liquidity and investor activity.

### 1. Vodafone Idea

Vodafone Idea remained one of the most actively traded stocks on the NSE as investors continued to monitor developments related to the telecom company’s business and fundraising initiatives. The stock has consistently featured among high-volume counters in recent trading sessions.

### 2. Motherson Sumi Wiring India

Motherson Sumi Wiring India also witnessed significant trading activity. The company operates in the automotive wiring harness segment and remains closely tracked due to its exposure to India’s growing automobile industry.

### 3. YES Bank

YES Bank continued to attract strong investor participation and remained among the highest traded banking stocks by volume during the session. Banking stocks generally remained active amid improving market sentiment.

### 4. Suzlon Energy

Suzlon Energy featured among the most traded stocks as renewable energy companies continued to attract market attention. The stock frequently ranks among the highest-volume counters due to strong retail participation.

### 5. Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC)

IRFC was another actively traded PSU stock on Thursday. Investors continue to watch railway-related companies amid ongoing infrastructure development initiatives.

### 6. Ashok Leyland

Commercial vehicle manufacturer Ashok Leyland also featured among the day’s most traded stocks as automobile stocks remained active during the session.

items.title: Volatility over value: High-beta counters outshine blue-chips as retail investors swarm India’s stock market
items.author: Pavan Burugula, Swaraj Singh Dhanjal
items.text:
# ANALYSIS Volatility over value: High-beta counters outshine blue-chips as retail investors swarm India’s stock market

The largest corporations by market cap are no longer the ones commanding the biggest retail shareholder bases, instead high-swing counters with rapid price momentum are dominating the popularity chart.

 Pavan Burugula & Swaraj Singh Dhanjal October 22, 2026 / 15:02 IST 

 

Stock markets

- Retail investors favor high-beta stocks over mega-caps.
- Yes Bank and Vodafone Idea attract massive retail bases.
- India now has 73 companies with over 1M shareholders.

On Dalal Street, sheer market size is no longer the magnet for retail capital. In an aggressive hunt for direct alpha stocks, India’s individual investors are increasingly bypassing traditional mega-cap heavyweights in favor of volatile, high-beta swing stocks that offer sharp price movements.

As a result , the largest corporations by market capitalization are no longer the ones commanding the biggest retail shareholder bases. Instead, high-swing counters which have long been popular for their rapid price momentum are dominating the popularity chart, as per date from Prime Database.

The best example for this trend is the private lender Yes Bank whose stock has undergone at least seven cycles of steep rise and correction in last five years. It is the second largest company in terms of number of shareholders.

While its market capitalisation is just Rs 51,000 crore, it has over 58.44 lakh retail investors as on June 30, data showed. In contrast, HDFC Bank, India’s largest private sector lender, has only 45 lakh investors while State Bank of India(SBI), India’s largest public sector lender, has only 39 lakh retail investors, data showed. HDFC Bank has a market cap of Rs 10.7 trillion, while SBI's market cap stands at Rs 8.9 tillion.

Vodafone Idea is another example of a high volatility stock widely owned by retail investors. The company has over 58 lakh investors, marginally behind Yes Bank and is the third largest Indian company in terms of number of shareholders.

Sulzon Energy has about Rs 53,000 crore market capitalisation but has more retail investors in its cap table than most of the Nifty companies. Suzlon Energy currently has 55 lakh retail investors as of June quarter making it the fifth largest Indian company in terms of number of shareholders. In the last four years, the company has added over 30 lakh new retail investors, data showed.

Indian Railway Finance Corp(IRFC), a public sector entity, is another key favourite stock amongst retail punters. Since its listing in early 2021, IRFC stock moved in cycles of abrupt rises and falls. The company had just 18 lakh retail investors as of June 2022 but now it has risen to 50.86 lakh , data showed.

“Over the past two years, we have seen retail participation in equities rise, alongside an increase in demat accounts. Two key drivers are financialisation and digitalisation, which have improved access to the markets. An army of new retail investors has entered the market. Social media has also helped spread information about the markets. Together, these factors have supported greater retail participation,” said Kranthi Bathini, director of equity strategy at WealthMills Securities.

Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles leads the charts with 62 lakh retail investors in the company. In June 2022, the company was the fourth largest in terms of retail shareholders with 35 lakh investors meaning the company roughly doubled its retail shareholder base since 2022. Tata Motors, which was recently demerged from Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles too has 55 lakh retail investors. Tata Steel also features in the top 10 with over 51 lakh retail investors. To be sure, Tata Motors and Tata Steel are not as volatile as other stocks favoured by retail investors.

Interestingly, ITC which has traditionally been a popular retail stock, seems to have fallen out of favour with 41 lakh retail investors as of June. In FY22, it had 30 lakh retail investors meaning its retail shareholder base has increased by less than 40% -- the slowest amongst the top 20 companies. ITC stock has faced massive headwinds in the recent past with stock losing 30% in 2026 so far, data showed.

...

Market experts note that retail investors are taking matters into their own hands as returns from leading mutual funds have softened over the past two to three years. Consequently, average retail shareholder counts across the top 1,000 listed companies jumped from 2.5 lakh in June 2022 to 3.5 lakh by June 2026.

items.text:
# Trending Stocks Today, October 19, 2026: PC Jeweller, Vodafone Idea, Yes Bank, PNB In Focus

Authored By HDFC SKY | Last Modified: Oct 19, 2026 02:15 PM IST

₹15.80 -1.56%

Mumbai, October 19: PC Jeweller, Vodafone Idea, Yes Bank and Punjab National Bank (PNB) were the most traded stocks by volume on the NSE on Monday, October 19, as company-specific developments drove activity. PC Jeweller surged 13.76% after Cupid chief Aditya Kumar Halwasiya bought a stake in the company, while PNB gained 4.81% after reporting better-than-expected Q2 earnings. Vodafone Idea slipped 1.03% amid ongoing concerns over its financial position despite appointing a new COO, while Yes Bank fell 1.66% as investors weighed profit growth against the potential impact of the Supreme Court’s AT1 bond ruling.

...

## PC Jeweller Limited (up 13.76%)

Shares of PC Jeweller surged on Monday, October 19, extending their rally over two trading sessions after Aditya Kumar Halwasiya, chairman and managing director of Cupid, acquired a stake in the jewellery retailer through a bulk deal. The buying interest comes as PC Jeweller completes its transition to a debt-free company, while investors also track its September-quarter business update and upcoming earnings announcement.

The sharp gains followed a purchase of 5.10 crore PC Jeweller shares by Halwasiya for approximately Rs 73.59 crore. The transaction was executed at an average price of Rs 14.43 per share.

...

## Punjab National Bank (up 4.81%)

Shares of Punjab National Bank (PNB) surged on Monday, October 19 after the state-owned lender reported better-than-expected September-quarter earnings. The rally prompted brokerages to raise their price targets, citing stronger net interest income, expanding margins and improving asset quality. PNB reported a 13% year-on-year increase in net profit to Rs 5,532 crore for Q2 FY27, while net interest income rose around 11% to Rs 11,601 crore. The bank’s gross non-performing asset ratio improved by 90 basis points to 2.55%, reinforcing investor confidence in its earnings outlook.
